name: Esketamine
route_note: Nasal spray self-administered under direct supervision in a certified healthcare setting with 2 hours' monitoring; IV as an anaesthetic in some countries.

discovery.by: Berman, Krystal and colleagues (Yale), later Zarate (NIMH)
discovery.note: Small trials of IV racemic ketamine showed rapid antidepressant effects (2000, 2006), prompting Janssen to develop the S-enantiomer as a nasal spray.

tagline: Nasal-spray S-ketamine for treatment-resistant depression, given under supervision
summary: Esketamine is the S-enantiomer of ketamine, developed by Janssen as a nasal spray for treatment-resistant depression and for depressive symptoms with acute suicidal ideation. It acts within hours to days rather than weeks, but must be given under medical supervision because of sedation, dissociation and abuse potential.
mechanism: Esketamine is a non-competitive NMDA receptor channel blocker with about twice the affinity of racemic ketamine. Blockade of NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons is thought to cause a surge of glutamate release, AMPA receptor activation, BDNF release and mTOR-dependent synaptogenesis in the prefrontal cortex.

These rapid changes in synaptic connectivity are proposed to underlie its fast antidepressant onset, although the exact mechanism, including possible roles of metabolites and opioid systems, is still debated.
uses: Treatment-resistant depression in adults (with or without an oral antidepressant)
Depressive symptoms in adults with major depressive disorder with acute suicidal ideation or behaviour (with an oral antidepressant)
Anaesthesia and analgesia (IV, some European countries)

history.title: Anaesthetic
history.detail: Esketamine is marketed as an anaesthetic (Ketanest S) in Germany.

history.title: Ketamine signal
history.detail: Berman and colleagues report rapid antidepressant effects of IV ketamine.

history.title: NIMH trial
history.detail: Zarate and colleagues confirm rapid response in treatment-resistant depression.

history.title: Breakthrough designation
history.detail: The FDA grants breakthrough therapy designation to intranasal esketamine.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Spravato is approved in March 2019 for treatment-resistant depression with an oral antidepressant; EU approval follows in December.

history.title: Suicidal ideation
history.detail: The FDA approves use for depressive symptoms with acute suicidal ideation or behaviour.

history.title: Monotherapy
history.detail: The FDA approves Spravato as monotherapy for treatment-resistant depression in January 2025.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 to noresketamine

safety.boxed_warning: Risks of sedation, dissociation, respiratory depression, abuse and misuse; available only through a restricted REMS programme; suicidal thoughts and behaviours.

facts: Spravato was the first antidepressant with a novel mechanism approved by the FDA in decades.
Patients may not drive until the next day after a dose.
